turns.human_input: I just got laid off this morning, completely out of nowhere. My mortgage is due in 8 days, car payment in 12, and I have maybe $900 in checking. I have a wife and two kids. I don't even know where to start. What should I do?!
turns.ai_response: Start today, not tomorrow. First: file for unemployment online right now — most states take 2-3 weeks to process so every day you wait costs you. Second: call your mortgage servicer before you miss a payment and ask specifically about forbearance; lenders are legally required to discuss options, and proactive contact gets you better outcomes than calling after you've missed. Third: call your auto lender the same way — ask for a payment deferral. Most will say yes once. Your $900 buys you more time than you think if you move fast. What state are you in? And do you have any severance or a final paycheck coming?

turns.human_input: Texas — no severance, they said it was a restructuring. But I do have two weeks of PTO they owe me, that's maybe $1,800. I didn't know I could call the mortgage company before missing a payment — that actually makes sense. Filing unemployment now while we talk.
turns.ai_response: Good move filing while we talk — don't stop. Texas is an at-will state with no state severance law, but that PTO payout is legally owed and you should confirm it in writing before your final day. That $1,800 plus the unemployment bridge buys you real runway — call the mortgage servicer today, before the payment is missed.

turns.human_input: Unemployment filed. I'm calling the mortgage servicer next, then the auto lender. I've already texted three former colleagues about contract work. I've got a list, I'm working it.
turns.ai_response: That's a solid response under pressure — you've covered the immediate obligations, opened the income replacement lanes, and your wife is already moving. The contract outreach is the right instinct; former colleagues who know your work are your fastest path back to income. You're in a hard spot but you're executing well.
